title: Knights of Peter Claver, secret societies and the Masons
summary: Mitchell's Catholic order versus social and pleasure clubs, with wake guards and comparison to Masons' degrees.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Is the knife of Peter Clever, is that like the masons?

Well, it's a Catholic order. Oh, a Catholic order, I didn't realize that. Yeah, it's a Catholic order. You have to be Catholic to be a knight of Peter Clever. That's the hall there on Orleans Street, between Durham and the Roman, on that side of the bank. It used to be the old French hospital.
Yeah. Yeah, we bought that building there, bought that old square ground. I'm sure.
But what's the difference between a secret society like that and a club like the San Jacinto?
Well, they had the secrets and the old secrets.
In the organization.
They all revealed it. Yeah. Just the members of the organization know the secrets, you know.
And the San Jacinto didn't have anything like that.
No, no, no. It was a social and pleasure club.
A club, yeah.
Yeah. And when it says social and pleasure, it was a social and pleasure. Yeah.
It's hard for me to understand that because I don't think they have clubs like that in other parts of the country. Well, you see a... It's original in New Orleans.
Well, when you see a... On a night of a wake, you'll see the Knights of Peter Clever. God in the bottom. God in the bottom of the soul on each side of the corner of the corner.
One at the foot and one at the head.
They sit up all night?
Oh, well, they had... Members had different tones. They'd... Around about 10 minutes. They really keep away. 10 minutes or 15 minutes, something like that.
Yeah. You know, long... See, they stand in one position, so... Oh, yeah. You'd be relieved, relieved.
Oh, yeah. They can't stay there.
They'll be relieved every so often, see. It's like the mason that have the body guarded. Really?
I didn't know that, at the wake. I didn't know that, I knew that they go to the great heart.
When I die, you come see. Oh yeah? Harold, are you going to die?
You're not going to die. You're still a mason?
All my life.
Oh, I didn't know that.
I mean it's just the same, it's just different, like say, in a religion, you know, but now they got Catholics belonging to the mason.

Well sure, well nobody, well nobody never told me against no, nothing against no religion when I joined a mason. No one had never told me nothing against the Catholic religion. We don't have, we don't have the one cause. Everybody serves that same God.

You serve them in a different way, you know. But outside of that, you know. It all serves the same God. You see the masons, the masons have 33rd, 33rd, 33rd degree. Well us, our high degree resembles that, but we called it the 4th degree. Yeah. You know, you don't have...
You call it the 4th degree?
Yeah, well that's the highest. You're equal as a mason, a mason, but they use that number, say the 33rd degree, or we called it the 4th degree. Well that represents that high in the same way.
